messages:
eli: Quick heads-up for docs owners: starting next Monday we'll switch quickstart samples to use ephemeral sandbox keys instead of plaintext placeholders (no more YOUR_API_KEY in examples). This reduces accidental key leakage and lets the docs runner validate requests against a mock backend.

maria: Nice. Will this break existing READMEs / installs for external contributors?

eli: We designed it to be backward-compatible for users who just copy/paste the code, but maintainers will need to run the migration helper to add the new header metadata. Two main changes: 1) replace placeholder strings with templated env var references, and 2) add `runner: sandbox` to the snippet metadata. Example: 

```
<!-- redwood:example {"language":"js","entry":"quickstart.js","runner":"sandbox","vars":{"API_KEY":"${{REDACT}}"}} -->
```

eli: And in the sample code we recommend reading the key from env: `const key = process.env.REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;` so local devs still work.

karen: Where's the migration helper? can it touch README.md files in repos?

eli: Yes, tool is repos/docs-tools/sandbox-migrate. Usage: 

```
# dry run
python -m redwood_docs.sandbox_migrate --path docs/ --dry-run

# apply (creates backups)
python -m redwood_docs.sandbox_migrate --path docs/ --apply --backup
```

eli: The tool will annotate snippets and swap inline placeholders for `${{REDACT}}` wrapped vars. It will NOT change example logic or add network calls.

maria: How will CI handle this? our doc-preview tests currently hit staging and expect real network responses.

tj: We'll add a docs CI matrix: `docs:server` will run with `REDWOOD_SANDBOX=true` and start the local mock. Tests that require live external integrations will be skipped under sandbox. Maintainers can opt into full integration runs with `DOCS_INTEGRATION=true`.

karen: Any changes needed in SDK repos (js/py/go) to support sandbox runner?

eli: Minimal. We added a tiny shim in SDK samples: `redwood-docs-client` exposes `createClient({key, sandbox: true})` which swaps endpoints. We'll publish patch releases for JS/Py/Go tomorrow morning. That lets docs examples call the same functions but talk to the mock backend when `sandbox:true`.

docs-bot: Policy doc published: https://git.redwood.example/docs/policies/sandbox-keys.md  Please review. The migration tool v0.1 is here: https://git.redwood.example/docs-tools/pkgs/sandbox-migrate (run dry-run before apply).

maria: Cool. I'll carve out time Friday to run the tool on integrations repo and open PRs. tagging owners in the PR description.

tj: If anyone hits flaky mock responses, file a docs-qa ticket and cc @tj. We'll add a health-check endpoint in the mock to reduce flakiness.

eli: TL;DR checklist for owners: run sandbox-migrate, update snippets to include `runner:sandbox`, replace plaintext API placeholders with `${{REDACT}}` vars, add `REDWOOD_SANDBOX` job to docs CI if you rely on preview tests. Ping me or @karen for help. :wave:
